message.text: Looking into what records the store layer deletes before the memo row itself during API deletion.
Reading `Store.DeleteMemo` in `store/memo.go` to identify dependent records deleted before the memo row.

The question targets the store layer's deletion sequence for memos.

`Store.DeleteMemo` in `store/memo.go` deletes memo relations where the memo is source or target, then attachments, then the memo row itself. The analysis now checks whether `DeleteAttachment` cascades further and whether reactions or memo shares are also removed recursively.

package store

import (
	"context"
	"log/slog"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"

	"github.com/pkg/errors"

	"github.com/usememos/memos/internal/base"
	"github.com/usememos/memos/internal/storage/s3"
	storepb "github.com/usememos/memos/proto/gen/store"
)

type Attachment struct {
	// ID is the system generated unique identifier for the attachment.
	ID int32
	// UID is the user defined unique identifier for the attachment.
	UID string

	// Standard fields
	CreatorID int32
	CreatedTs int64
	UpdatedTs int64

	// Domain specific fields
	Filename    string
	Blob        []byte
	Type        string
	Size        int64
	StorageType storepb.AttachmentStorageType
	Reference   string
	Payload     *storepb.AttachmentPayload

	// The related memo ID.
	MemoID *int32

	// Composed field
	MemoUID *string
}

type FindAttachment struct {
	GetBlob        bool
	ID             *int32
	UID            *string
	CreatorID      *int32
	Filename       *string
	FilenameSearch *string
	MemoID         *int32
	MemoIDList     []int32
	HasRelatedMemo bool
	StorageType    *storepb.AttachmentStorageType
	Filters        []string
	Limit          *int
	Offset         *int
}

type UpdateAttachment struct {
	ID        int32
	UID       *string
	UpdatedTs *int64
	Filename  *string
	MemoID    *int32
	Reference *string
	Payload   *storepb.AttachmentPayload
}

type DeleteAttachment struct {
	ID     int32
	MemoID *int32
}

	thumbnailCacheFolder = ".thumbnail_cache"
	motionCacheFolder    = ".motion_cache"

Store.DeleteMemo appears to delete only one record type before the memo row itself.

The store layer deletes memo_relations by MemoID and by RelatedMemoID, plus attachments, before removing the memo row. The API layer also recursively deletes child comment memos first.

Store.DeleteMemo deletes memo_relation records where this memo is either memo_id or related_memo_id, and attachment records via DeleteAttachment. Reactions and memo_share are not deleted in this method.

API comment memos are deleted recursively via Store.DeleteMemo calls, not by the store layer directly. No triggers or other cleanup mechanisms were found.

Examining the store layer's DeleteMemo implementation to identify which related records are deleted before the memo row itself.

Store.DeleteMemo removes memo_relations where the memo is either the source or target, plus attachments, before deleting the memo row itself. Comment memos are handled recursively through the same store path.

The API recursively deletes child comment memos through Store.DeleteMemo before deleting the parent memo. This occurs outside the parent's own store cleanup.

The answer is memo_relation and attachments, referenced in store/memo.go. Reactions and memo_share are not deleted at the store layer.
